transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, I came in because... lately I've just been taking on way too much, I think. I went from barely even settling into my new apartment to suddenly saying yes to all these mentoring sessions. And for work, I started taking on extra client prototypes, plus I decided to completely redesign my whole portfolio. 

It was just... it was like I had to fix my entire life in one huge sprint, and I'm realizing it's a bit much.
How long has this period of taking on so many extra projects and feeling like you needed to overhaul everything been going on for?
Um, it's been about a month. This whole intense up-and-down pattern... it's really been going on since I moved into the new apartment.
During this past month, have you noticed that you need much less sleep than usual but still feel full of energy the next day?

Yeah, actually. Um... for several nights there, I slept maybe three or four hours. But I woke up convinced I was totally fine. I just figured I should use the extra time to get ahead on all those projects.
During this past month, have you experienced any unusual beliefs that others might find strange, or seen or heard things that others don't seem to notice?

No, no, nothing like that. I haven't heard voices or seen anything that wasn't there. And I don't think I've had any, um, strange beliefs or anything. I just felt really driven to get all that work done, but I wasn't imagining things.

Have you ever had a period in the past—lasting a week or more—where you felt unusually high, energetic, or 'on top of the world,' or conversely, a period of deep depression, low energy, or loss of interest in things?

Yeah, definitely the deep depression. Um, the heavier depressive stretches have actually been showing up since my separation... which was about 11 months ago. So those low periods started even before this latest move made everything feel a lot sharper.

During this past month when you were taking on all these extra projects and sleeping very little, did it cause any serious problems—like conflicts with clients, missed deadlines, or trouble at work—or did people around you notice you weren't acting like your usual self?

Yeah, it actually has caused some issues. I mean, I was doing all this work, but I ended up completely missing a major design review at work. And... honestly, I've just been avoiding my friends and family lately. I feel pretty embarrassed about how scattered and unreliable I've seemed to everyone.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a distinct period of approximately one month characterized by increased goal-directed activity (taking on multiple new projects, redesigning portfolio, mentoring sessions), decreased need for sleep (3-4 hours with no fatigue), and inflated confidence/energy. This has caused clear functional impairment (missed major work deadline, social withdrawal, embarrassment). No psychotic features (hallucinations or delusions) were present, ruling out F31.2. Critically, the patient endorses a prior distinct period of significant depressive symptoms (low energy, loss of interest) beginning approximately 11 months ago following a separation, confirming a bipolar course rather than a single manic episode (ruling out F30.1). This pattern of at least one manic episode plus a prior major depressive episode meets criteria for Bipolar I Disorder, current episode manic, without psychotic features.
